name: Grouper Prep
smallware: Scale, cutting board, 1 full size 4" SS pan, 1 Full 4" perforated pan, Ice Bags, Day portion bags
steps: Weigh and record the starting weight of the Grouper.
Check the grouper for pin bones by running your gloved hand over the grouper.
Trim the Grouper.
Cut the belly from the grouper.
Look for and remove any parasites.
Trim the tail end piece off the grouper.

Using a sharp knife, cut the grouper into the desired number of sandwiches, dinners, and nuggets. The tail-end piece should always be a sandwich portion. Nuggets should be cut from any piece that is overweight.
Once cut, put the Grouper into bags of 5 sandwiches or dinners per bag.
Label and date, refrigerate and rotate
**Include all waste, ceviche, nuggets, sandwiches, and dinner portions on your Grouper Sheet for tracking**
Grouper Weights:
Dinners 7.9 - 8.5w/oz
Sandwich Portion are 5.5oz - 6.0oz
Nuggets 5.5 w/oz.

name: Chilean Seabass Thaw /Prep
steps: Pull Thaw a case and remove each piece from its bag
Set each piece in a perforated pan with a drip tray underneath
Cover and let sit until completely thawed
Once thawed, the water has been completely drained.
Weigh each piece separately before cutting; they will vary in thickness and size.
If they weigh under 6 oz, cut another piece with a similar thickness into 3 pieces. Place one cut piece with the whole piece and portion into a date bag
If the piece is thin, match it up to another thin piece. If the piece is thick, match it up to another thick piece.
Put all portions into a labeled & dated pan, place in the cooler
Notes: Place extra cut pieces (if any) into the smallest portion bags to use them up.
Portions range in weight from 6.0 oz to 6.5 oz. Don’t cut anything if you don’t have to.

name: Caesar Salad Bulk
steps: Before opening the bag, look for discolored or wilted pieces
If questionable, ask a manager to look at it before opening
Do not toss out without the Manager looking at it first
The salad person needs to remove any wilted or discolored pieces before use
With Spinner:
Take 24 romaine hearts
Cut the Core from each, and remove outer leaves (if discolored) and discard
Cut remaining leaves into 1" cuts
Fill the sink halfway with water and a half bucket of ice. Add the Fruit & Veggie Wash to the water 0.25oz. Per gallon of water (Read the label), and stir to dissolve
Add chopped Romaine, let sit for 2 to 3 minutes
Mix to get any dirt removed from the leaves
Lift into the basket, let it drain for 1 to 2 minutes
Place into the Salad spinner and spin for a minute, drain excess water from the spinner
While draining water, shake the basket to remove lettuce from the walls
Put the top on and do step #6 again
Remove the slotted basket, and portion into lemon bags
Label, date, and store in the cooler, above any raw foods
NO SPINNER:
Take 24 romaine hearts
Cut the Core from each, and remove outer leaves (if discolored) and discard
Cut remaining leaves in 1" cuts
Rinse and drain in Lexan with holes into another Lexan without holes to catch water
Label, date, and store in the walk-in cooler, above any raw foods

name: Red Fish & Grits
steps:
Sautee
	Sauce
	1. In a sauté pan over medium heat, add Cajun butter and pepper mix
	2. Once the butter is melted add heavy cream and green onion
Reduce sauce for 2-3 minutes while stirring/tossing in pan

Grill
	Fish 
	1. Take a portion of Redfish baster with garlic butter and add blackening seasoning 
	2. Place fish on flattop and cook for 3-4 minutes depending on thickness
	3. Flip fish and cook for additional 2 minutes
If the fish still has skin on, peel off as much as you can.

Oven 
	Grits
	1. Place it in oven at 450-500°F for 2-3 min until fully heated
Plate in large bowl

Build
	1. Oven station places grit cake in a large bowl 
	2. Grill station hands fish to oven when fully cooked
	3. Oven places fish on grits and hands to sautee
Sautee pours sauce over dish and passes to expo

Expo:
Garlic bread

Plateware: Large bowl

name: Ribeye Steak (SI)
steps: Generously top with steak seasoning
Cook on a char grill to the desired temperature.
Brush finished steak with room temperature garlic spread.
Make sure the spread is melted before serving
Rare - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125–130°F
Medium Rare - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130–140°F
Medium - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140–150°F
Medium Well - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any pink, 150–160°F
Well done - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Expo: Steak knife, requested sides

Place chicken strips on the grill with the buttered side down for 4 minutes and then flip for 3 more minutes or until the chicken internal temperature reaches 165°F.

name: Filet Mignon (SI)
steps: Generously top with steak seasoning
Place on chargrill for 2 minutes
Rotate the steak 90degrees and cook for 2 minutes to make cross marks
Flip the steak and grill for 2 minutes
Place the steak on a pizza tray and place it in 450°F oven
Follow the time guide below for cooking times
Brush finished steak with room temperature garlic spread.
Make sure the spread is melted before serving
Rare - 4 minutes in oven - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125–130°F
Medium Rare - 5 minutes in oven - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130–140°F
Medium - 7 minutes in oven - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140–150°F
Medium Well - 8 minutes in oven - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any pink, 150–160°F
Well done - 10 minutes in oven - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Note: Times may vary on the cut of the steak. Steaks ordered med-well and well will be butterflied unless the guest does not want it.

name: Avocados (fresh) (bar & grill)
steps: Received:
When received, check the Avocados to make sure they are ripe enough to sell.
If they are soft and a darker green to black color, then they should be ripe.
If they are ripe, set them in the cooler with the receiving date on them.
If the case is not ripe, then it is best to leave them out of the cooler in a safe, clean place. With the receiving date on them. Once they start to ripen, place them in the WI cooler.
Cutting instructions:
Take a sharp knife and carefully cut into the avocado long ways until you hit the pit.
Start to spin the avocado, keeping the blade on the pit.
Take the knife out and split the avocado in half.
Remove the pit with a spoon.

Pick the knife up and carefully cut the avocado while holding the skin side in your hand (or peel the avocado with a spoon and then cut into slices). Once cut, use a spoon to pull out the pieces or slices.

steps: Wash the tomato under cold running water.
Carefully place the upright tomato against the blades, push the handle towards the blades, creating 3/8" slices.

name: Caesar Salad Bulk
steps: Before opening the bag, look for discolored or wilted pieces
If questionable, ask a manager to look at it before opening
Do not toss out without the Manager looking at it first
The salad person needs to remove any wilted or discolored pieces before use
With Spinner:
Take 24 romaine hearts
Cut the Core from each, and remove outer leaves (if discolored) and discard
Cut remaining leaves into 1" cuts
Fill the sink halfway with water and a half bucket of ice. Add the Fruit & Veggie Wash to the water 0.25oz. Per gallon of water (Read the label), and stir to dissolve
Add chopped Romaine, let sit for 2 to 3 minutes
Mix to get any dirt removed from the leaves
Lift into the basket, let it drain for 1 to 2 minutes
Place into the Salad spinner and spin for a minute, drain excess water from the spinner
While draining water, shake the basket to remove lettuce from the walls
Put the top on and do step #6 again
Remove the slotted basket, and portion into lemon bags
Label, date, and store in the cooler, above any raw foods
NO SPINNER:
Take 24 romaine hearts
Cut the Core from each, and remove outer leaves (if discolored) and discard
Cut remaining leaves in 1" cuts
Rinse and drain in Lexan with holes into another Lexan without holes to catch water
Label, date, and store in the walk-in cooler, above any raw foods

name: Salad Mix
steps: Before opening the bag, look for discolored or wilted pieces
If questionable, ask a manager to look at it before
Do not toss out without the manager's okay
The salad person needs to remove any wilted or discolored pieces before mixing with Spring Mix
NEW cutting procedure for cutting whole heads
Cut & Remove any bruised or wilted parts of romaine & leaf lettuce
With a knife, cut Romaine & Leaf Lettuce.
Starting from the core, leaving the core intact,
Cut completely through from the base through the top.
Now make a 1/4 turn, and cut through from the base through the top.
Now cut across the head into 1"-1.5" sections.
This will cut the lettuce into bite-sized pieces for the guests.
Place the cut lettuce into an ice bath to remove any dirt for 2 minutes
Remove any Head cores as well
Add the salad mix to the spinner
Spin & drain 2 or 3 times to remove as much water as possible.
And the mixture is as dry as possible
Weigh out and place in Lemon bags
Spinach check, and remove any wilted or bruised leaves
In a separate portion bag, add a 5-ounce portion of Spinach to each bag
Tie the Spinach bag shut.
Now place the spinach bag in with the salad mix bag and …
Tie shut, date, and place in the cooler above any raw foods
Cut the Product and combine in a large Cambro and mix thoroughly.
Once combined, label and date.

name: Pasta Linguine
steps: Combine water, salt, and oil in a 12-quart (4-gal) stock pan over medium heat.
Bring water to a boil.
Add pasta to boiling water, and return water to a boil.
Immediately stir the pasta to prevent it from sticking together or to the bottom of the pot.
Cook for about 7 minutes once boiling again, or until pasta is al dente (cooked but still firm to the touch).
Remove from heat and drain.
Take two sheet pans and split the pasta, add 6oz of Scampi sauce on each tray, and mix with the pasta.
Take two more sheet pans and fill them with ice. Put the sheet pan with the pasta on top in the ice.
When the pasta is completely cooled down, portion into Lemon bags
Label, date, rotate, refrigerate in cooler above any raw foods
Good detached oyster, w/no cuts

name: Mango Salsa

ingredients.name: Jalapeno (good size)
ingredients.unit: Ea. Stem removed, seeded, and diced), = 6oz

steps: Cut off the bottom half to 2/3s of cilantro stems (either throw away, or pick good for expo line), rough chop the top part of cilantro with skinny stems and mainly leaves, and add to the mix
In a large mixing bowl
Add Mango, Jalapenos, and Pico, gently mix with a rubber spatula
Add salt, pepper, and cilantro, mix
Squeeze lime over the top of the mixture, and mix
Transfer to a lemon bag, label, and date.
Place in the cooler, rotate old product to the front
Remove stems and seeds from jalapeños and dice into ¼" pieces.
Peel a red onion and dice into ¼" pieces.
Place diced mango into a bowl
Add diced jalapenos with stems and seeds removed.
Add 8oz of red onion.
Add pineapple and orange juice, as well as the juice from 1 lime
Add salt, and grind 6 twists of black peppercorns into the salsa.
Add remaining ingredients and stir well.
Place in 4" - 1/2 pan
Label, date, rotate, and refrigerate

name: Coconut Rice
smallware: Rice cooker, can opener, rubber spatula, 3 full sheet pans, kitchen spoon, rubber spatula, lemon bags
steps: 5/30/24 using 48oz cans, still 16oz of Cream of Coconut
Rice Cooker Method:
Add coconut milk and Rice to the rice cooker
Close lid and cook for 20-25 min. Unplug cooker
Add a can of Cream of Coconut, and stir, let stand for 10 min.
Lay out on a sheet pan and let cool down in the cooler until 40 degrees
Portion into three bags
Label, date, and store in the cooler
Note: Please store any unused cream of coconut in an appropriate container with a label and date.

name: Crab Roll Meat Portions (Cold)
smallware: mixing bowl, rubber spatula, lemon bags, 8oz deli containers, and lids
steps: New 2.5# packaging of Crabmeat
Take a 2.5# bag of Alaskan crab meat and remove it from its packaging.
Drain the meat and empty it into a large mixing bowl. LIGHTLY press the water out of the whole leg pieces and set aside. Now do the same with the small meat pieces
Add 12 volume oz. of Hellman's mayo
Fold crab meat and mayo until combined.
Make sure not to break up the crab meat when mixing.
Portion the whole leg pieces evenly into 8oz8-ozli containers,
NOW -Place an EMPTY 8-oz deli container on the scale and Zero it out.
Now, place a container with the whole leg on the scale, and top off with the small/ broken meat mixture, bringing it up to the 4.25oz weight.
Label the lids and date them.
Place all 8 portions into a large lemon bag, tie off, label, date, and rotate.
Take 1# of Alaskan crab meat and remove it from its packaging.
Drain the meat and empty it into a large mixing bowl
Add 6 volume oz. of Hellman's mayo
Fold crab meat and mayo until combined.
Make sure not to break up the crab meat when mixing.
Portion the mixture evenly into 4- 8oz deli containers, lid them, and label them.
Place all portions into a large lemon bag, tie off, label, date, and store.
You should yield 4 portions out of the 1 lb. of crab.

Portion broccoli to 3.5oz in a small bag

Label, date, and refrigerate

name: Crab Bairdi
smallware: scale, red mesh bags, bucket,
steps: ***For the best prepping results -
The crab needs to be sitting out at room temp for at least an hour, you want to be able to easily remove clusters without breaking them apart
**Never use a knife to break clusters apart
Important NOTE: If a Cluster weighs under 11oz, place it to the side to see if any other broken pieces or smaller clusters show up.
Use those to make weight for another portion.
(BE Sure to cut completely through the knuckle from the piece you're trimming)
Instructions:
Portion crab into net bags (11 - 13oz each) 11.5oz dockside
If one cluster weighs between 11-13oz, just portion the whole cluster into a red bag
Place portions back into the box with the lid
Label how many portions are in the box on the outside (Side & top) with a Sharpie
Date and store back in the freezer.

steps: Open 3 cans of tomatoes, peeled
Take the tomatoes out of the can and put them in the Robo-coupe (save the tomato juice left in the cans)
Blend lightly, just until there are no big chunks but still somewhat thick, and pour into a large Cambro.
Chop garlic in the Robo-Coupe
Chop basil by hand finely with a knife
Put all contents into Cambro (including the rest of the tomato juice from the can of tomatoes, oil, garlic, basil)
Add salt and pepper and stir with a whisk
Portion into 2 (double the bags up) lemon bags.
Label, date, and refrigerate

steps: IN A LARGE STOCK POT OVER MEDIUM HEAT, START TO MELT THE CAJUN BUTTER WITH THE RED PEPPER

ONCE THE SAUCE HAS SIMMERED FOR A MINUTE OR 2, REMOVE FROM THE HEAT AND CAREFULLY POUR INTO THREE (3) DEEP THIRD PANS
To Heat Sauce Heat in microwave to around 200 degrees- uncovered (no wrap)
1/3 pan 6 minutes
1/6 pan 2-3 minutes
On the line, add Arrowroot for 1/3 pan (1 -4oz cup)
1/3 pan sauces- mix 4 oz arrowroot- 8 oz COLD water
1/6 pan sauces mix 1 oz arrowroot -2 ounces COLD water
1/3 pan 1 minute
1/6 pan- 30 seconds

name: Oysters New Orleans
steps: Shelf Life on frozen 1/2 shell: 1 day
These oysters are already shucked; just need to be lightly washed in salt water to have the grit removed and have the muscle detached
**Use 10 grams (10 grams = 1.5 teaspoons) of Morton salt per liter(33 oz) of cold water for salt water wash**
Make sure there is no shell in the oyster.
Cut the muscle off the bottom of the shell.
Very important **** keep the tag with the oysters and ensure you mark the last date sold on the tag.
Once all oysters are sold, bring the tag to the office and put it in the oyster tag box.
**Do not stack prepped more than 3 high in a storage container with a logo deli in between each layer.**
Bad Oyster (Dry looking)
New Orleans Oyster prep
Melt Cajun butter slightly so that it can be brushed onto oysters.
**monitor total oyster amount to not melt too much Cajun butter**
Lightly coat with parmesan cheese.

name: Oyster Fresh Shucked
steps: **If a good oyster gets cut or ripped in the shucking process, it is ok to use it for the baked applications**
**Cover oysters in ice during the shucking process to help them open more easily and keep within a temperature of 41°F or below **
**If needing saltwater rinse, then mix 10 grams = 1.5 teaspoons of Morton salt per 1 liter of cold water**
Cleanly shuck oysters. Mark on the sheet the quantity of usable oysters you yielded.
Make sure there isn't any shell in the oyster.
If there is grit or shell on the oyster, lightly wash in a saltwater mix
Cut the muscle off the bottom of the shell.
Very important****keep the tag with the oysters and ensure you mark the last date sold on the tag.
Once all oysters are sold, bring the tag to the office and put it in the oyster tag box.
Must use fresh oysters within 2 weeks of harvest date
**Do not go by use the date!!**
Once you feel the top muscle is cut clean finish opening the oyster
Start tip of knife in between top of oyster
Twist once leveraged to pop it open
Once popped start sliding knife down side keeping tip pointed up towards top shell to cut that muscle connection
Pics of Bad Oysters below
Bad Oyster, shrunken, dehydrated, and stuck to shell
Throw away and will be negated during production
Visible grit and a little shell
Will need a light rinse
Cut during opening, still fresh just light rinse and can be used for baking applications
Good oyster, pick that little spec at top and ready for use
Rinse in Salt water

name: Pizza Dough Balls (bar & grill)
steps: Preparation:
Take the dough ball out of the freezer
Take a dough ball out of the bag
Pull out the wrap long enough to cover both sides of the dough ball
Now with the pan spray, spray, on both under and on top of the dough ball
Cover the dough ball with the wrap to make a pocket, leaving about 2 inches around the ball so it can expand
Place 12 dough balls per sheet pan
Label the pan with the date and time, and each dough ball with a day dot
Put the tray on the bottom of the speed rack (move the other trays up one so that you pull from the top pan first)
Leave it in the walk-in cooler, preferably for 48 hours before you pull it out of the walk-in cooler, unless you need it sooner.
Wed and Thursdays are the days you would wrap the most since they take two days to thaw and wouldn't be ready for use until Friday and Saturday
Saturday and Sunday should be the days you do the fewest because they wouldn't be ready until Mon and Tues (our slowest days)
Pull out from the walk-in what you need for the whole day and let it sit out for an hour or so, or until it starts to rise or proof up, and then put it in the pizza cooler
Don't wait until it is completely proofed before you put it away, or it will continue to proof in the cooler until it cools
Time and Temperature will dictate how long it should be left out

If you are out of dough and it is Frozen it will take about 7 or 8 hours at room temperature until it proofs and can be used (do not put under or on direct heat). If you need it first thing in the morning, it can be left out over night as long as it is not more than 7 or 8 hours and also at 75 degrees or cooler.

steps: Take a 5# bag of Alaskan crab meat and remove it from its packaging. Drain the meat (+ any whole legs leftover from crabmeat portions).
Sort the whole legs from the shredded / pieces of meat, keeping them in separate containers
Press the water out of the whole leg pieces and set aside. Now do the same with the small meat pieces
In a mixing bowl. Add the piece of meat, then add 24 volume oz. of Hellman's mayo
Fold crab meat and mayo until combined.
Make sure not to break up the whole crab meat legs when mixing.
Portion the whole leg pieces evenly into 8oz deli containers, (No less than 2 or 3 whole legs)
NOW -Place an EMPTY 8-oz deli container on the scale and Zero it out.
Now, place a container with the whole leg on the scale, and top it off with the small/ broken meat mixture, bringing it up to the 4.0oz weight.
Label the lids and date them.
Place all 8 portions into a large lemon bag, tie off, label, date, and rotate.

name: Grouper Prep
smallware: Scale, cutting board, 1 full size 4" SS pan, 1 Full 4" perforated pan, Ice Bags, Day portion bags
steps: Weigh and record the starting weight of the Grouper.
Check the grouper for pin bones by running your gloved hand over the grouper.
Trim the Grouper.
Cut the belly from the grouper.
Look for and remove any parasites.
Trim the tail end piece off the grouper.

Using a sharp knife, cut the grouper into the desired number of sandwiches, dinners, and nuggets. The tail-end piece should always be a sandwich portion. Nuggets should be cut from any piece that is overweight.
Once cut, put the Grouper into bags of 5 sandwiches or dinners per bag.
Label and date, refrigerate and rotate

Sandwich Portion are 5.5oz - 6.0oz
Nuggets 5.5 w/oz.

name: Oysters Crabbyfellars
steps: Shelf Life - on frozen 1/2 shell: 1 day
These oysters are already shucked; they need to be lightly washed in salt water to have grit removed and have the muscle detached
**Use 10 grams(=1.5 teaspoons) of Morton salt per liter of cold water for a saltwater wash.**
Make sure there isn't any shell in the oyster.
Cut the muscle off the bottom of the shell.
Very important****keep the tag with the oysters and ensure you mark the last date sold on the tag.
Once all oysters are sold, bring the tag to the office and put it in the oyster tag box.
**Do not stack prepped more than 3 high in the storage container with the logo deli in between each layer**
Crabbyfellars Prep shown BELOW
Top Oysters with Garlic Spread,
Then top with Crab & Spin dip

name: Polenta Cakes
smallware: stock pot, whisk, rubber spatula,
steps: In a stock pot, bring the vegetable stock to a boil
Slowly stir in Polenta and continuously stir while cooking for 5 to 6 minutes
Once polenta is cooked, add the cheese, whisk to incorporate
After the cheese is melted in, add the house spice and the heavy cream
After all is combined, pour out of the pot and use the rubber spatula to scrape the sides and bottom. Do not scrape the product stuck to the bottom of the pot.
Spreading out the mix onto a half sheet tray, and gently shake the pan to level it out.
Place in cooler (2hrs.) or freezer (1hr) to firm up, before portioning.
Once Polenta is firm use the grid to cut into 20 pieces
**this recipe will make 10 orders of shrimp n grits**

Place the whole cleaned head into a cleaned sink.
Pour the rinse solution to cover the item
Remove and let drain for roughly 5-6 minutes.
Cut the whole head in half from the core end.
Lay the flat side of the 1/2 of head onto the cutting board and cut in half through the core again. Giving you 4 equal quarters.
Now remove the core section by holding the knife at a 45° degree angle
Now slice the cabbage thin, for use and bag accordingly

name: Avocados (fresh) (bar & grill)
steps: Received:
When received, check the Avocados to make sure they are ripe enough to sell.
If they are soft and a darker green to black color, then they should be ripe.
If they are ripe, set them in the cooler with the receiving date on them.
If the case is not ripe, then it is best to leave them out of the cooler in a safe, clean place. With the receiving date on them. Once they start to ripen, place them in the WI cooler.
Cutting instructions:
Take a sharp knife and carefully cut into the avocado long ways until you hit the pit.
Start to spin the avocado, keeping the blade on the pit.
Take the knife out and split the avocado in half.
Remove the pit with a spoon.

Pick the knife up and carefully cut the avocado while holding the skin side in your hand (or peel the avocado with a spoon and then cut into slices). Once cut, use a spoon to pull out the pieces or slices.

name: Crust /Cook / Cut
steps: Forming the crust:
Take the dough ball out of the dough bag
Place the dough ball in a bowl of flour and lightly dust both sides, shaking off any excess flour, then lay flat on the table
Form an outer crust by pressing down with your fingers about an inch away from the edge of the dough ball, all around until the outer crust is formed
Once the outer crust is formed, push down on the inside area of the crust with the bottom of your fingers (not the tips), working towards the outside until evenly flat
Pick up the dough and make a fist with both hands under the flattened dough while stretching and turning the dough until the crust has an even thickness and is the size of the pizza screen
Place on the screen (stretch if needed) until the dough is at the edge of the screen.
Only push down on the outer edge, not the mesh part of the screen
Topping the pizza:
Spread red sauce evenly over the inner crust, starting from the middle and working towards the outer crust (do not sauce the outer crust)
Leave some sauce in the ladle to add to any spots needing more sauce
Add a pinch of salt and pepper evenly on the sauce (not on the crust)
Add mozzarella cheese starting at the edge of the inner crust and working towards the middle, spreading evenly
Cooking instructions:
Place in oven ( 500-515 degrees) on the screen for approx. 6 minutes, depending on the oven
Take the pizza off the screen when possible and continue to cook for another 2-3 minutes or until the crust is golden brown, spinning occasionally for even cooking
Cutting the pizza:
Once golden brown, take the pizza out of the oven and put it on a deli paper-lined 14" metal tray
Make 4 equal cuts, cut again to make 8 triangular slices
Finishing spices/sauces after cutting:
Sprinkle Romano cheese evenly over the cheese
Plateware: 14" Deli Lined Pizza Tray

name: Pasta Shrimp Scampi
steps: Sauté shrimp pieces in a medium sauté pan on high heat, with Scampi Butter for approximately 3 minutes, or until shrimp are cooked and scampi reduced.
Heat pasta in boiling water for approximately 1 minute.
Add tomatoes to the existing pan of shrimp
Add the drained pasta.
*If the sauce is still a little too thick to toss, adding a little heavy cream to thin it is ok*
Flip the pasta a couple of times to makes sure all the pasta is coated with the sauce.
Pour finished pasta into a large bowl.
Sprinkle with parmesan cheese evenly across the top
Expo: Cuban Bread, soup spoon

name: Pasta Seafood
steps: Take 3 scallops and lay them flat, then filet horizontally in half
Take shrimp pieces and put them into the sauté pan with the scallops
Add scampi sauce, cook for 4 minutes, and turn often

Add 1- 6 oz ladle red sauce to scampi sauce in sauté pan
Heat pasta in boiling water for approximately 1 minute.
Add Pasta to the existing pan of shrimp and sauce.
Flip the pasta a couple of times to make sure all the pasta is coated with the sauce.

name: Pasta Cajun Chicken Alfredo
steps: Note: **If using flat top, baste chicken with garlic spread before cooking**
Evenly season the chicken breast with blackening seasoning.
Place the chicken breast on the chargrill, seasoned side down. After 4 minutes, flip and cook an additional 3 minutes. Cook the chicken until the internal temperature reaches 165°F.
In a medium sauté pan on high heat, add Cajun butter, and alfredo sauce, and heat for approximately 2 minutes.
Place 1 portion of pasta in the pasta water for approximately 1 minute, and drain
Add drained pasta to the Cajun butter pan. Toss
Flip the pan a couple of times to make sure everything is coated with the sauce
Pour finished pasta into a large bowl.

Sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese evenly across the top

*If the sauce is still a little too thick to toss, adding a little heavy cream to thin it is ok*

name: Steak & Crab
steps: Steak Preparation:
Generously top with steak seasoning
Cook on a char grill to the desired temperature.
Brush the finished steak with 1oz. of warm garlic spread.
Rare - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125–130°F
Medium Rare - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130–140°F
Medium - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140–150°F
Medium Well - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any, pink 150–160°F
Well Done - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Crab Preparation:
STEAMED:
Place crab portions into a boiling pot of water or the steamer.
Cook for approximately 5 minutes.
Pull and drain water off the crab before plating
GRILLED/ FIRE ROASTED:
Place the drained boiled crab on a large sizzler pan.
Coat generously with garlic spread and Old Bay,
Place in oven for 2 to 3 minutes or until seasoning is golden brown

name: Boil Crab Boil
steps: NOTE: Served with either Cajun Sauce or **Scampi Sauce is (GLUTEN FREE)
CLASSIC = 1 portion bag of each item
JUMBO = 2 portion bags of each item
Crab Preparation:
Steamed:
Place 1- 3/4 # crab portions (one cluster for CLASSIC)/ ( JUMBO -2 crab portions) into the pot of water.
Cook for approximately 5 minutes
Check the knuckle of the crab to make sure it is hot
Place the crab in a lemon bag on a beer tray and add the entire contents to the bag over the crab
Fold the bag over so the steam stays in the bag, and give it to the expo to finish.
Sausage Cook Prep:
Take one or two 4-oz links and cut on a bias almost the whole length of the sausage.
Grill on the flat top, approx. 2 minutes per side.
Note: You can pre-grill the sausage and place it in the cooler to be reheated with the shrimp in the seafood stock water.
Boil Sauces: (EXPO)
SCAMPI STYLE = SCAMPI SAUCE (GLUTEN FREE) 6oz
CAJUN STYLE = 6oz CAJUN SAUCE

name: Fish/Crab/Chicken Cooking Method
steps: FISH:
NOTE: When seasoning a fish for serving, be sure to baste and season the presentation (flesh) side of fish. Not the Skin side.
GRILLED / BLACKENED:
Baste fish with garlic spread and then lightly and evenly dust with Requested seasoning.
Place on flat top. After 4 minutes, flip and cook approx. 3 minutes.
When fish is finished cooking, brush with garlic spread to moisten before plating.
BROILED:
Place fish on a broil pan and cover with water.
Baste the fish with garlic spread, evenly and lightly dust with Old Bay
Place in oven for approx. 5 minutes.
When fish is finished cooking, brush with garlic spread to moisten before plating.
FRIED:
Place fish into milk wash and drain the excess.
Transfer to breading and shake off the excess, making sure to cover the fish thoroughly.
Transfer fish to fryer for approx. 5 minutes or until golden brown and cooked thoroughly.
Transfer from fryer to Sav-A-Day to drain excess oil.
STEAMED:
Place crab portions into boil pot or steamer.
Cook for approximately 5-7 minutes.
Pull and drain all liquid from crab, back into the pot before plating
GRILLED / FIRE ROASTED:
Place drained boiled crab on large sizzler pan.
Coat generously with garlic spread and old bay seasoning
Place in salamander for 1 minute or 450-500°F degree oven for 2 to 3 minutes or until seasoning is golden brown. Do not allow to burn
FLAT TOP:
Baste the chicken breast with garlic spread and season with Requested Seasoning.
Place on flat top and cook for 3-4minutes,
Turnover over and continue to cook for additional 3-4 minutes
Lightly baste with garlic spread before plating
CHAR GRILL:
Take Chicken breast and just season with Requested Seasoning.
Place skin (Smooth) side down on grill cook for 2 minutes, turn 45° degrees
Cook 2-3 minutes more to give the diamond design on the breast,
Turnover and cook 2 -3 minutes more to complete cooking
Lightly baste with garlic spread before plating

Place the mesh bag portion of uncooked shrimp into boiling Old Bay water

Place the mesh bag portion of uncooked shrimp into boiling Old Bay water

Let shrimp stand in ice water until completely chilled.
Remove cooked shrimp from the mesh bag and arrange evenly on a plate, retaining some liquid.
Sprinkle shrimp with Old Bay seasoning

Sear Tuna to rare temp on flat top for 1.5 minutes per side.
Place 2 scoops coconut rice in bottom of a serving bowl, flatten with back of scoop
Slice the seared Tuna, thin into 4 pieces and place atop the rice.
Fill 1st corner of the bowl with cabbage.
Fill another corner with shredded pineapple salsa.
Fill a third corner with avocado salsa.
In the last corner add 3 wonton Chips.
Expo:
Pour Soygave on meat only,
Drizzle lime crema over all ingredients
Top with green onion & Lime wedge
Plateware: Medium Square Bowl

name: Ribeye Steak (SI)
steps: Generously top with steak seasoning
Cook on a char grill to the desired temperature.
Brush finished steak with room temperature garlic spread.
Make sure the spread is melted before serving
Rare - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125–130°F
Medium Rare - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130–140°F
Medium - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140–150°F
Medium Well - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any pink, 150–160°F
Well done - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Expo: Steak knife, requested sides

name: Pineapple Chicken Teriyaki
steps: Place 2 marinated chicken breasts on the grill
Cook for 2 minutes and rotate 45 degrees to get grill marks
Cook another 2 minutes and then flip over

Cook another 3-4 minutes until internal temp is 165°F
As the chicken is finishing, place a pineapple on the flat top for 1 minute to heat it up
Place the pineapple wheel on top. Then onto a bed of rice
Then place the chicken on the pineapple
Baste the chicken with the pineapple sauce and serve

name: Filet Mignon (SI)
steps: Generously top with steak seasoning
Place on chargrill for 2 minutes
Rotate the steak 90degrees and cook for 2 minutes to make cross marks
Flip the steak and grill for 2 minutes
Place the steak on a pizza tray and place it in 450°F oven
Follow the time guide below for cooking times
Brush finished steak with room temperature garlic spread.
Make sure the spread is melted before serving
Rare - 4 minutes in oven - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125–130°F
Medium Rare - 5 minutes in oven - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130–140°F
Medium - 7 minutes in oven - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140–150°F
Medium Well - 8 minutes in oven - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any pink, 150–160°F
Well done - 10 minutes in oven - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Note: Times may vary on the cut of the steak. Steaks ordered med-well and well will be butterflied unless the guest does not want it.
Expo: Steak knife, requested sides

Rare - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125–130°F
Medium Rare - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130–140°F

Medium Well - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any, pink 150–160°F
Well Done - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F

name: Twin Tails
steps: Cutting the Tail:
Cut the shell from front to rear, being careful that you do not cut too deeply.
Pop open the bottom segment closest to the tail.
Pull meat out of the shell, still leaving the tail attached. Place the lobster meat on top of the shell.
Make a 1/4'' incision down the center of the lobster tail.
Fan the lobster's tail fins out
Cooking:
Place the lobster tails on a broil pan and fill with water to above where the tail fin stops
Baste the top with garlic spread
Place in a 450-500°F oven for approximately 6 minutes
Remove from the oven and with a knife, make a (2) 1/4" incision running lengthwise with the tail across the meat to let the heat get in and speed up the cooking process.
Now re-baste with garlic spread, lightly dust with Old Bay.
Return to oven for approximately 4- 5 minutes until lobster tail is cooked

Rare - 4 minutes in oven - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125–130°F
Medium Rare - 5 minutes in oven - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130–140°F
Medium - 7 minutes in oven - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140–150°F
Medium Well - 8 minutes in oven - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any pink, 150–160°F
Well done - 10 minutes in oven - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Note: Times may vary on the cut of the steak. Steaks ordered medium well and well done will be butterflied unless the guest requests not to be butterflied.

name: Waffle Cone and Bowl
steps: 2oz volume ladle.

Batter: Mix the 5lb bag of batter with 4.5 cups of water. This is one cup less that the direction on the bag state. Whisk water into the batter. If needed you can add up to an additional half cup of water for a thinner pancake like consistency. If you use the full 5.5 cups of water the cones tend to crack as the batter gets too thin.
Turn the waffle iron on to 4.5.
Allow to fully heat. It will beep when it’s ready.
Open first side of waffle iron and spray with pan coat aerosol spray.
Ladle 2 volume ounces of batter onto the iron and close firmly.
Set timer if needed.
If making additional cones repeat above steps on the other side of waffle iron.
Allow the cone to cook until light golden color forms. This will be about 3 minutes.
For a cone:
Using tongs, remove the cone gently and place on the waffle roller pad.
Insert the cone turner into the cylinder of the roller pad and rotate the cone which will bend the cone around the form.
For a bowl:
Using tongs, remove the cone gently and place on top of the open side of a 16oz deli cup.

Using a paper coffee cup or similar size, press the bottom of the cup gently into the center of the cone. This will force the cone down into the deli cup and allow the cone to harden into a bowl shape.
Allow the cone to sit for a minute to hard and remove cone.
Remove other cooking waffle cone and repeat.
Store cones and bowls in a food storage bin and date.
Waffle Cone Dip/Sprinkle a Cone or Bowl:
Take a hardened cone and dip into chocolate cone dip in straight down motion. Submerge about ¼ inch past the fold line of the cone.
Lift out and hold for about 10 seconds allowing excess to drip off.
Dip one more time to same depth and lift out.

If adding sprinkles, add them immediately after removing from chocolate the second time. Please cone over a sheet tray with logo paper and shake sprinkles over the entire chocolate area until fully covered. Excess sprinkles can be put back in tub.
Place cone on to a ¼ sheet tray with logo paper chocolate side down to fully harden.

name: FOAMING Instructions
steps: On the LavAzza Machines Milk (Steamer) Frothing
Cappuccino - use the 3 (SSS squiggly lines) on the left side of the machine
Latte - use the 2 (SS squiggly lines) just to the right of the Cappuccino
Purge the steam wand and clean the steam wand before using.
Clip the Thermometer to the side of the metal milk jug
Add milk to the metal milk jug per recipe.
Hold the jug in the palm of your hand (not by the handle) so you can feel the temperature on your hand
Tilt milk jug to the side to create a vortex and the milk will swirl to evenly steam, keeping the wand close to the top of jug to make your FOAM.
Place the steam wand closer to the surface for cappuccino foam and slightly lower for latte foam
Drop the steam wand down to the bottom of the milk jug after foaming and warm the entire bottom of the jug. It is finished when it is almost too hot to hold, and the temperature reaches 150 degrees
Remove the milk jug and clean the steam wand and purge the steam wand
Give the milk jug some hard taps on the counter surface to destroy large bubbles and swirl the milk to get distinct layers of foam

When pouring into coffee drink pour directly in the center to break the surface and mix the products. When properly tapped and swirled the steamed milk will come out first to mix with the coffee and the foam will come out on top.
**Prepare Your Milk**: Start with cold, fresh milk. Whole milk typically produces the creamiest foam, but you can also use 2% or skim milk depending on your preference.

**Fill the Milk Pitcher**: Pour the desired amount of milk into the stainless steel pitcher. Remember that milk expands when steamed, so only fill it about one-third full for a single latte and slightly more for multiple drinks.
**Purge the Steam Wand**: Before steaming the milk, purge any condensation or residue from the steam wand by briefly opening the steam valve for a few seconds into a drip tray or cup.

**Position the Steam Wand**: Place the tip of the steam wand just below the surface of the milk in the pitcher. The wand should be at a slight angle and positioned off-center to create a whirlpool effect.

**Start Steaming**: Turn on the steam wand. You'll hear a hissing sound as steam begins to flow. Hold the pitcher with one hand by the handle and use your other hand to control the angle and position of the wand as well as to monitor the temperature of the milk.

**Texture the Milk**: Lower the pitcher slightly to introduce air into the milk (the tip of the wand should be hovering just above the surface of the milk), creating small bubbles. This process is called "stretching" or "texturing" the milk. You should hear a gentle hissing sound as air is incorporated. You will texture the milk for about 10 seconds for lattes/ and about 15-20 seconds for cappuccinos.
**Monitor Temperature**: As the milk begins to warm, gradually raise the pitcher to submerge the steam wand deeper into the milk.

**Froth the Milk**: Continue steaming until the milk reaches the desired temperature, typically between 140°F and 160°F. You can gauge the temperature by touch or use a thermometer inserted into the pitcher. If you are relying on touch, the desired temperature is met when you can't keep your hand on the pitcher for more than a couple of seconds without it burning.
**Turn Off the Steam Wand**: Once the milk reaches the desired temperature, turn off the steam wand by closing the steam valve.
**Wipe and Purge**: Wipe the steam wand with a damp cloth to remove any milk residue. Then, purge the steam wand again to clear any remaining milk.
**Tap and Swirl**: Tap the pitcher gently on the counter to break up any large bubbles, then swirl the milk to incorporate the froth throughout.
**Pour and Serve**: Pour the steamed milk into your prepared espresso shot to create a latte or cappuccino.
**Enjoy**: Your latte is ready to enjoy!

**Pour and Serve**: Pour the steamed milk into your prepared espresso shot to create a latte or cappuccino.

FOAMING INSTRUCTIONS:
Purge the steam wand and clean the steam wand
Clip the Thermometer to the side of the metal milk jug
Add milk to the metal milk jug per recipe.
Hold the jug in the palm of your hand (not by the handle) so you can feel the temperature on your hand
Tilt the milk jug to the side to create a vortex, and the milk will swirl to evenly steam the milk, keeping the wand close to the top of the jug to make your FOAM.
Place the steam wand closer to the surface for cappuccino foam and slightly lower for latte foam

Drop the steam wand down to the bottom of the milk jug after foaming and warm the entire bottom of the milk container. It is finished when it is almost too hot to hold, and the temperature reaches 150 degrees
Remove the milk jug and clean the steam wand and purge the steam wand
Give the milk jug some hard taps on the counter surface to destroy large bubbles and swirl the milk to get distinct layers of foam

When pouring the foam into the coffee drink, pour directly in the center to break the surface and mix the products. When properly tapped and swirled, the steamed milk will come out first to mix with the coffee, and the foam will come out on top.

Generously top with steak seasoning

Flip the steak and grill it for another 2 minutes
Follow the time guide listed below for cooking times
Brush finished steak with room temperature garlic spread.
Make sure the spread is melted before serving
Rare - 4 minutes in oven - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125-130°F
Medium Rare - 5 minutes in oven - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130-140°F
Medium - 7 minutes in oven - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140-150°F
Medium Well - 8 minutes in oven - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any pink, 150-160°F
Well done - 10 minutes in oven - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Note: Times may vary on the cut of the steak. Steaks ordered medium well and well will be butterflied unless the guest requests not to.

Cutting the Tail:
Cut the shell from front to rear, being careful that you do not cut too deeply.
Pop open the bottom segment closest to the tail.
Pull meat out of the shell, still leaving the tail attached. Place the lobster meat neatly on top of the shell.
Make a 1/4'' incision down the center of the lobster tail.
Fan the lobster's tail fins out
Cooking:
Place the lobster tail on a broil pan. Baste the top with garlic spread
Season with Old Bay Seasoning
Add water to above where the tail fin stops.
Place in oven for approx. 6 minutes
Remove from the 450-500°F oven. With a knife, make a (2) 1/4 inch incision running lengthwise with the tail across the meat to let the heat get in and speed up the cooking process.
Return to the oven for approximately 5 minutes until the lobster tail is cooked

BROILED: Place the Salmon on a broil pan, and add water to the broil pan to keep from burning. Baste with garlic spread and lightly dust with Old Bay. Place in a 450-500°F oven for approx. 5-6 minutes. Brush with garlic spread to moisten and plating. Place the Salmon on a toasted bread

steps: Lightly dust the burger with Montreal seasoning. Place the Hamburger on the chargrill

Rare - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125-130°F
Medium Rare - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130-140°F

steps: Baste the Tuna with garlic butter and evenly sprinkle with Blackening seasoning.
Place seasoned side on the flat top and let cook 2 minutes

Place fish on a dressed ciabatta roll,
The expo will top with a drizzle of Cusabi dressing
Expo: 1 oz drizzle of cucumber wasabi, Lemon wedge, LTO if requested, side requested

Place Grouper Cheeks into flour, then into Beer Batter.
Place in the Sav-A-Day and sell to the fryer

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through (165°F).
Transfer to Sav-A-Day to drain excess oil.
Place the grouper on the bottom of the slider buns.

Place the bun in a lined round basket and send it to the fry station

name: Tail 8oz & Crab Cake
steps: Cutting the Tail:
Cut the shell from front to rear, being careful that you do not cut too deeply.
Pop open the bottom segment closest to the tail.
Pull meat out of the shell, still leaving the tail attached. Place the lobster meat on top of the shell.
Make a 1/4'' incision down the center of the lobster tail.
Fan the lobster's tail fins out
Cooking:
Place the lobster tail on a broil pan and fill with water to above where the tail fin stops
Baste the top with garlic spread
Place in a 450-500°F oven for approximately 6 minutes
Remove from the oven and re-baste with garlic spread, lightly dust with Old Bay
With a knife, make a (2) 1/4" incision running lengthwise with the tail across the meat to let the heat get in and speed up the cooking process.
Return to oven for approximately 4-5 minutes until lobster tail is cooked
When finished cooking, brush with garlic spread to moisten before plating.

Pull meat out of the shell, still leaving the tail attached. Neatly place the lobster meat on top of the shell.
Make a 1/4'' incision down the center of the lobster tail.
Fan the lobster's tail fins out
Cooking:
Place the lobster tail on a broil pan and fill with water to above where the tail fin stops
Baste the top with garlic spread
Place in a 450-500°F oven for approximately 6 minutes
Remove from the oven and re-baste with garlic spread, lightly dust with Old Bay
With a knife, make a (2) 1/4" incision running lengthwise with the tail across the meat to let the heat get in and speed up the cooking process.
Return to oven for approximately 4-5 minutes until lobster tail is cooked
When finished cooking, brush with garlic spread to moisten before plating onto a lined 1/4 tray.
Expo: 2oz butter, lemon wedge, 2 sides
Plateware: Lined 1/4 Tray

Filet:
Generously top the steak with seasoning
Place on the chargrill for 2 minutes
Rotate the steak 90° and cook the steak for another 2 minutes, to make cross marks.
Flip the steak and grill for another 2 minutes
Place the steak on a pizza tray and place it in a 450°F oven
Follow the time guide underneath for cooking times
Brush finished steak with room temperature garlic spread.
Make sure the spread is melted before serving
Rare - 4 minutes in oven - a cool red center; pink otherwise 125-130°F
Medium Rare - 5 minutes in oven - a warm red center, otherwise pink 130-140°F
Medium - 7 minutes in oven - warm pink center, otherwise brown 140-150°F
Medium Well - 8 minutes in oven - mostly brown with a gray center, very little, if any pink, 150-160°F
Well done - 10 minutes in oven - Brown throughout with no sign of pink >160°F
Note: Times may vary on the cut of the steak. Steaks ordered medium well and well will be butterflied unless the guest does not want it.
Expo: steak knife, 2 sides, 2oz butter, lemon wedge

name: Fish (Haddock) & Chips
steps: Note: If the batter is too thick, the center of the filet will not cook thoroughly. (A light-medium pancake batter consistency)
Take 2 pieces of haddock filets.
Lightly dust the Haddock in the flour. Shake off excess.
Place the Haddock into the beer batter. Make sure it is completely covered in beer batter
Carefully move closer to the fryer with the batter container, now lift the fish, letting some of the excess to drip off
Cooking in a 350°F fryer for approx. 4 minutes or until golden brown and fully cooked.

While holding the end of the piece of fish into the fryer and slowly dipping the battered fish in the fryer, waving it back and forth, letting the batter firm up slightly before letting it go (so the pieces don't stick to the bottom or the side of the basket).
When you have 3/4 of the piece formed into a crust, let it go, and repeat the step.
Remove from fryer.

Plate accordingly

FRIED:
